newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Prominent Russian businessman joins Sibneft board.
newsitem.headline: Prominent Russian businessman joins Sibneft board.

text.p: Boris Berezovsky, a Russian businessman whose interests range from cars to television, has been elected to the board of Russia's sixth largest oil company Sibneft, a Sibneft spokesman said on Friday.

Berezovsky was voted in at a shareholders meeting on Thursday at the headquarters of OAO Sibirskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Sibneft), Alexander Vikulov told Reuters from the Siberian city of Omsk, where the meeting took place.
"Berezovsky was elected to the board, because he is also chairman of Neftyanaya Finansovaya Kompaniya (NFK), which currently holds 51 percent of Sibneft," Vikulov said.
NFK and Stolichny Bank Sberezhnii took control of 51 percent of Sibneft under the government's shares-for-loans scheme last year with a bid backed by Bank Menatep.
Oil analysts and the Russian media had speculated that Berezovsky was behind the previously unknown NFK, but Vikulov's comments were the first official confirmation.
The chief executive of Russian gas monopoly RAO Gazprom, Rem Vyakhirev, also joined the board of Sibneft as representative of the Russian government.
The spokesman said Sibneft chairman and president Viktor Gorodilov would remain chairman of the nine-member board.
Sibneft is one of a dozen vertically integrated Russian oil groups created over the last few years. Its main operating unit is Noyabrskneftegaz.
